title: sophia-martin-optimize-evals-review-prep-notes
content:
Meeting prep: Optimize / Evals review (quality regression triage)

Meeting date: 2026-03-03 10:30 AM (1:1 with Aisha)
Objective: go over recent eval run that surfaced regressions on prompt-set A and summary of A/B test between model-v1 and model-v2. Decide next experiments and owners.

Background:
- Eval run: eval-run/2026-02-20 (full dashboard linked above). We ran ~2.3k examples across 5 prompt buckets (A-E).
- A/B: model-v1 (baseline, full-precision) vs model-v2 (quantized + kernel-change). v2 was rolled to dedicated pool on 2026-02-22.

Key observations (from quick pass):
- Pass@1 (prompt-set A) dropped from 82% -> 76% (absolute -6pts) on v2.
- Factuality error rate (human label) increased 4.3% -> 9.1% (x2) on prompt-set A and subset of B.
- Latency improved by ~18% p50 on v2 (good), but tail latency unchanged.
- Tokenization mismatch? A small set of failures show odd token splits for named entities (e.g., "Pfizer-BioNTech" -> "Pfizer- -BioNTech") that correlate with hallucinations.
- Prompt sensitivity: prompt paraphrases (shorter prompt) show smaller regression; longer prompts amplify the drop.

Suspected causes / hypotheses:
- Quantization profile for attention kernels introduced approximation errors for long-context tokens.
- Tokenizer update in runtime pipeline (recent patch) changed split behavior for hyphenated names.
- Prompt engineering: v2 may be more sensitive to prompt phrasing due to altered logits distribution at generation start.

Quick check list before meeting (what to bring):
- Top 20 failure examples (samples.json exported) with model outputs + references + human labels.
- Diff of tokenization for failed examples (old vs new tokenizer) - need script output.
- A/B details: exact config used for v1 vs v2 (temp, top_p, presence_penalty, quant profile).
- Eval dashboard (pass/fail by prompt bucket, scatter plots).

Proposed experiments (short-term):
1) Rerun small set (n=200) of prompt-set A with v2 but old tokenizer (if possible) to test tokenization hypothesis — Owner: Jamie (due 2026-03-05).
2) Rerun using v2 with alternate quant profile (less aggressive) to see if factuality recovers — Owner: Noah (due 2026-03-06).
3) Prompt-robustness test: generate 5 paraphrases per example and compute variance in pass-rate — Owner: Sophia (me) (due 2026-03-08).
4) Collect 50 human-labeled cases focused on named-entities & hyphenation to validate error type — Owner: Aisha (due 2026-03-07).

Action items (from this prep):
- Jamie: export tokenization diffs + top 20 failures (2026-03-05).
- Noah: set up quick rerun with alternate quant profile + share results (2026-03-06).
- Aisha: coordinate 50-label HITs and add label schema for factuality/hallucination (2026-03-07).
- Sophia: run paraphrase robustness script, produce summary table (2026-03-08).
- All: quick sync 2026-03-09 to decide rollout (canary rollback vs config tweak).

Notes / conversation starters for 1:1 with Aisha:
- How urgent is rollback risk from CS side? Any live customer complaints referencing hallucinations?
- Should we pause v2 autoscaling bursts until we have tokenization hypothesis validated?
- If quantization is root cause, what's the tolerance tradeoff (latency vs 1-2% factuality loss)?

Open questions:
- Can the runtime serve v2 with the old tokenizer without a full rebuild? (tech blocker?)
- Are there known kernel bugs introduced in the recent optimization PR? PR #489 linked.
- Is there a simple temperature/tok limit that mitigates hallucinations without blowing up cost?

Misc notes / scribbles:
- Consider adding a short "sanity prompt" in the pipeline for named-entity preservation (e.g., tell the model to "preserve exact tokens in entity spans").
- If we need a rollback, prefer config toggle at routing layer so we can route to model-v1 by policy.

End of prep notes. Will refine after 1:1 and push an action-email summary.
